video_title: Thunder Buddies podcast: What's next for OKC after missing NBA Finals with loss to Spurs?

quotes.speaker: Joe Mussatto
quotes.summary_phrase: Thunder would have won the series if healthy
quotes.excerpt: If they had one of AJ Mitchell or Jalen Williams, I think the Thunder would have won the series.

text_blocks.speaker: Justin Martinez
text_blocks.text: That's kind of one of the big what-ifs with this series, right? Just what would this have looked like had both teams been at full strength?

text_blocks.speaker: Joe Mussatto
text_blocks.text: I think it's the most obvious what-if. As long as they're healthy, and I'm not even asking for full health, if they had one of AJ Mitchell or Jalen Williams, I think the Thunder would have won the series. I don't know that for sure, we can't know that for sure. If they had both of them, I'd feel really confident that the Thunder would have won.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mussatto
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs earned their series win despite Thunder injuries
quotes.excerpt: Credit the Spurs for seizing the opportunity. I don't want to make it sound like they only got past the Thunder because of injuries.
quotes.quote: Credit the Spurs for seizing the opportunity. I don't want to make it sound like they only got past the Thunder because of injuries. I mean, injuries played a part, but the Spurs also went out and won it and deserve to be there. And Jared McCain is thrust into a role in which he's the secondary creator behind Chet Holmgren.

quotes.speaker: Justin Martinez
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's impact on Chet Holmgren's performance
quotes.excerpt: It's a very tough matchup for him. Chet is somebody who's a play finisher, he gets a lot of his work done around the rim.
quotes.quote: Part of that obviously Victor Wembanyama, it's a very tough matchup for him. Chet is somebody who's a play finisher, he gets a lot of his work done around the rim. You got Victor Wembanyama down there, that's going to obviously make things more difficult. But there was just so much hesitancy, even on some looks that he got from deep where you don't have Victor Wembanyama closing out. He has the opportunity to shoot over some smaller defenders, he's passing them up and putting other guys in tougher positions where they have to now shoot some shots down the end of the shot clock or they're more contested.

quotes.speaker: Justin Martinez
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein's strong performance against Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Isaiah Hartenstein really impressed me this series. He held Victor Wembanyama to 23 for 43 shooting from the field.
quotes.quote: One guy who really impressed me was Isaiah Hartenstein this series. He held Victor Wembanyama to 23 for 43 shooting from the field, 53.5% in 33 minutes matched up with him. And then also showed a level of fearlessness on offense against him. He was constantly getting those floaters up there over him. He was aggressive there, obviously provided the playmaking, the rim protection.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mussatto
quotes.summary_phrase: Retaining Isaiah Hartenstein should be a top priority
quotes.excerpt: Retaining Isaiah Hartenstein should be number one on the Thunder's to-do list.
quotes.quote: Retaining Isaiah Hartenstein should be number one on the Thunder's to-do list. Because like you said, this is a matchup that we're going to see again, hopefully over and over again. And I think Hartenstein, no one's a Victor Wembanyama stopper, but he at least made things tough for Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Justin Martinez
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain's role and future with the team
quotes.excerpt: He's a real contributor for this team. He's not just a shooter, he's a very well-rounded scorer.
quotes.quote: Jared McCain, I think we were, that was a big question mark entering this postseason. He had some regular season success, especially like when he first got here when the team was very injured, they just needed to throw somebody out there. But it's like, okay, once this team gets healthy, once you get to the playoffs, what will his role look like? And I think we got the answer, like he's a real contributor for this team. He's not just a shooter, he's a very well-rounded scorer, he can get to the rim, he's got that little like bump middy. He does, he makes the right passes, he's obviously very limited defensively, but I thought made some hustle plays and was able to hold his own as best as he could.

quotes.speaker: Justin Martinez
quotes.summary_phrase: Chet Holmgren's performance and growth in Game 7
quotes.excerpt: Chet Holmgren did not have a great series by his standards, especially Games 1 through 6.
quotes.quote: Chet Holmgren did not have a great series by his standards, especially Games 1 through 6. Was shooting the ball poorly. I thought was getting some good looks, they just weren't falling. And after Game 6, he had said, it's too late now for me to change my game, I have to trust my work. And I feel like we really saw that in Game 7. I mean, he was the best player on the floor in that big moment, the the legacy game that a lot of people were kind of placing the title on for him. 35 points, nine assists, 12 for 21 shooting from the field, two for five shooting from deep, three turnovers, but I still felt like he was making the right plays, right decision-making, he was aggressive when he needed to be.

quotes.speaker: Justin Martinez
quotes.summary_phrase: Cason Wallace's defensive and offensive contributions
quotes.excerpt: Cason Wallace, I feel like really showed out. He shot 48.4% this postseason.
quotes.quote: It's worth giving a shout out to some of the guys like Cason Wallace, I feel like really showed out. He shot 48.4% this postseason, on top of everything he does defensively, 2.1 steals. He's somebody who definitely, he's up for that extension this summer. We'll see what that looks like, but I mean, he made strides the whole season, I feel like he stepped up in the postseason.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mussatto
quotes.summary_phrase: Cason Wallace's efficiency and defensive value
quotes.excerpt: Cason Wallace shot 50% from three, 18 of 36. And only Jared McCain and Alex Caruso took more threes than Cason Wallace.
quotes.quote: I'm glad you shouted out Cason Wallace. I mean, you mentioned his total playoff stats, but Spurs series, he shot 50% from three, 18 of 36. And only Jared McCain and Alex Caruso took more threes than Cason Wallace. So, I thought he was one of the guys and you don't expect like Cason Wallace to attack the the rim, but he was one of the guys who was very quick on, uh, retreating when Victor Wembanyama was under the basket.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mussatto
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs in five prediction for Western Conference Finals
quotes.excerpt: I have Spurs in five. I kind of have been wanting to back off that, you know, I'm not a very convicted man in my views.
quotes.quote: I have Spurs in five. I kind of have been wanting to back off that, you know, I'm not a very convicted man in my views, which is unfortunate given my occupation. But I'm sticking with Spurs in five. I think the more, more rest, especially the deeper the series goes, there's more days off, whereas like the conference finals were every other day. And I thought Victor Wembanyama was almost an every other game type guy as far as his energy. So I think that's going to really help them.
